lines.cap: He tipped so much gold in one city, he crashed their entire economy. For twelve years.
lines.say: He tipped so much gold in one city, he crashed their entire economy. For twelve years.

lines.cap: Mansa Musa. King of the Mali Empire in West Africa in the 1300s. His land had some of the biggest gold mines in the world.
lines.say: Mansa Musa. King of the Mali Empire in West Africa in the 1300s. His land had some of the biggest gold mines in the world.

lines.cap: In 1324, he made a pilgrimage to Mecca. And he did not travel light.
lines.say: In 1324, he made a pilgrimage to Mecca. And he did not travel light.

lines.cap: Reports describe thousands of people. Servants dressed in silk. Camels loaded with gold.
lines.say: Reports describe thousands of people. Servants dressed in silk. Camels loaded with gold.

lines.cap: When he passed through Cairo, he handed out gold to everyone. Officials, poor people, shopkeepers.
lines.say: When he passed through Cairo, he handed out gold to everyone. Officials, poor people, shopkeepers.

lines.cap: So much gold flooded the city that it lost its value. A historian who visited twelve years later said Cairo still hadn't recovered.
lines.say: So much gold flooded the city that it lost its value. A historian who visited twelve years later said Cairo still hadn't recovered.

lines.cap: On his way home, he tried to fix it, by borrowing gold back, at sky-high interest. Some say it's the only time one man controlled the price of gold in the Mediterranean.
lines.say: On his way home, he tried to fix it, by borrowing gold back, at sky-high interest. Some say it's the only time one man controlled the price of gold in the Mediterranean.
